title: Agile Analog delivers anti-tamper IP for ASPEED’s PQC-ready SoC
html:
Agile Analog has supplied a suite of analog security and power IP to ASPEED Technology for its AST1080 Platform Root of Trust (PRoT) system-on-chip (SoC). The IP has been successfully integrated into ASPEED’s second-generation, post-quantum cryptography (PQC)-ready chip, targeting next-generation data centers and cloud infrastructure.

The collaboration highlights the growing importance of mixed-signal IP in hardware security. It also demonstrates how configurable analog IP can help semiconductor designers address physical security threats while reducing integration complexity and development time.

Tackling physical silicon security threats

As data centers face increasingly sophisticated hardware attacks, protecting silicon at both the analog and digital levels is becoming a critical design consideration.

“Cloud service providers and enterprise datacenters face increasingly sophisticated security threats targeting physical silicon, such as voltage glitching, clock tampering, fault-injection and side-channel hardware attacks. Digital security alone cannot block these attacks. ASPEED integrated a set of mixed-signal hardware security sensors and power IP to further strengthen comprehensive physical anti-tamper capabilities of its AST1080 PRoT SoC,” said Chris Morrison, VP Product Marketing at Agile Analog.

The Cambridge, UK-based analog IP specialist supplied six IP blocks, including a voltage glitch detector, clock attack monitor, IR drop sensor and digital output temperature sensor. A capless internal low-dropout regulator (LDO) and real-time clock (RTC) help maintain power and system integrity.

The analog security sensors complement ASPEED’s digital security architecture, providing comprehensive physical anti-tamper protection.

Streamlining analog IP integration

Agile Analog used its Composa automated IP generation technology to configure the IP blocks to ASPEED’s specific process node, performance requirements and design rules. The approach helped reduce integration complexity and development time.

“Ensuring robust physical security in next-generation server platforms requires protection at both the analog and digital layers. Agile Analog’s range of security sensors and power IP has played a key role in enabling physical anti-tamper protection on our AST1080 PRoT SoC. The ease of IP integration and success on first silicon make Agile Analog a valuable partner as we drive open, resilient silicon security across cloud infrastructure,” said Charles Kuan, VP of Sales at ASPEED Technology.

First-pass silicon success

All six analog and mixed-signal IP blocks have been successfully validated in first-pass production silicon, marking a milestone for Agile Analog’s configurable IP technology.

“Physical anti-tamper protection is now a non-negotiable requirement for server management and security processors. Our analog security and power IP has integrated seamlessly into ASPEED’s high-density SoC design and this is performing flawlessly in the AST1080 silicon. Successfully proving six distinct analog/mixed-signal IPs in first-pass production silicon confirms Agile Analog as a trusted mixed-signal IP partner,” Morrison added.

The collaboration underscores the expanding role of analog security IP in semiconductor designs as cloud infrastructure providers prepare for emerging physical and quantum-era security threats.
